_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 1.12. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Officers plan to covertly follow a suspect in public places over several days to identify his associates. Which type of activity is this under RIPA 2000?
explanations: Correct: covert, specific operation, likely to obtain private information.

questions.scenario: PC FOX, on patrol, sees a man trying car door handles and watches him from a doorway for a few minutes before arresting him. Does this need a RIPA authorisation?
options: No – it is an immediate response to events

questions.scenario: A listening device is placed inside a suspect's private car. Which type of surveillance is this?
A device outside a house picks up conversations inside with the same quality as if it were inside. How is it treated?
explanations: Correct: same quality and detail as if on the premises.

questions.scenario: Which statement best describes a CHIS?
options: Any member of the public who calls the police
A person who establishes or maintains a relationship for the covert purpose of obtaining or disclosing information

questions.scenario: A neighbour, at police request, befriends a suspect to find out about planned burglaries. What is she?
options: An informant not covered by RIPA
explanations: She is doing more than witnessing.

questions.scenario: Every CHIS must have, under s. 29(5) RIPA (in general)…
options: a handler and a controller, and proper records

questions.scenario: Which is the usual police authorising officer for directed surveillance (non-urgent, no confidential information) (⚠ check edition)?
How long does a written directed surveillance authorisation last unless renewed or cancelled (⚠ check edition)?
How long does a standard (adult) CHIS authorisation last (⚠ check edition)?
Intrusive surveillance by police normally requires…
options: authorisation by the chief officer and prior approval of a Judicial Commissioner (except urgent cases)

questions.scenario: Which ground is available for intrusive surveillance?
Which is a ground for directed surveillance under s. 28(3)?
options: Preventing or detecting crime or preventing disorder

questions.scenario: Besides necessity, what else must the authorising officer believe?
options: That the activity is proportionate to what it seeks to achieve
That the suspect has previous convictions

questions.scenario: 'Collateral intrusion' refers to…
options: interference with the privacy of people other than the subject

questions.scenario: What is the effect of s. 27 RIPA when conduct is properly authorised?
options: It is lawful for all purposes
It cannot be challenged in court
explanations: Admissibility is still for the court.
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 1.12 · s. 27 – lawful for all purposes

questions.scenario: A town-centre CCTV system with clear signs records the public generally. Is this directed surveillance?
options: No – it is overt and general, not for a specific operation
explanations: Correct (though using it to covertly target a person in a planned way may need authorisation ⚠).

questions.scenario: Which article of the ECHR is mainly engaged by covert surveillance?
explanations: Fair trial (relevant to evidence, but not the main one).

questions.scenario: In an urgent case, a directed surveillance authorisation given orally lasts (⚠ check edition)…
Which person is LEAST likely to be a CHIS?
options: An undercover officer infiltrating a gang
An informant tasked to maintain contact with a dealer
A person tasked to befriend a suspect online
A member of the public who rings once to report a crime they saw
explanations: Correct: no covert relationship being used.

questions.scenario: What does 'status drift' refer to?
options: A change in a suspect's address
A member of the public gradually becoming a CHIS without authorisation

questions.scenario: Surveillance likely to obtain legally privileged or confidential information requires…
options: the same authorisation as any directed surveillance

questions.scenario: A juvenile CHIS authorisation lasts (⚠ check edition)…
Which law allows criminal conduct authorisations for CHIS in limited circumstances?
What should happen when an authorisation is no longer necessary?
Surveillance is 'covert' when…
options: it is carried out in a manner calculated to ensure the subject is unaware of it

questions.scenario: Officers watch a suspect's house covertly from a car parked in the street with binoculars for several days. Which is correct?
options: Intrusive, because it concerns a house
Directed, because they are not on the premises and the quality is not equivalent to being inside

questions.scenario: An undercover officer joins an online forum and builds a relationship with members to obtain information. Is this a CHIS?
options: No, online activity is never covered
Yes, it can be a CHIS (relationship maintained covertly)

questions.scenario: Which part of RIPA 2000 governs surveillance and CHIS?
An authorising officer considers whether the same information could be obtained by less intrusive means. Which test is this?
